selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What main comparison is made at the start of this passage?
questions.answer: Human beings are described as a small-scale reflection of the universe, and the opening chapter of the Qur’an is described as a compact example of the whole Qur’an.

questions.question: In that same pattern, how are the required prayers described?
questions.answer: They are presented as a broad yet concise summary of every form of worship.

questions.question: What does it mean to call the prayers an index?
questions.answer: It means the prayers gather many kinds of worship into one organized whole, the way an index points to many subjects in a compact form.

questions.question: What does it mean to call the prayers a sacred map?
questions.answer: It means the prayers guide a person toward understanding the different forms of worship found across creation.

questions.question: According to the passage, do the prayers point only to human worship?
questions.answer: No. They point to forms of worship belonging to all groups of created beings.

questions.question: How does the passage connect the relation between man and the universe with the relation between prayer and worship?
questions.answer: Just as man reflects the larger world in a small form, the prayers reflect the wider reality of worship in a concentrated form.

questions.question: What does the passage imply about the scope of the prescribed prayers?
questions.answer: Their scope is very wide, because they include meanings connected to all varieties and levels of worship.

questions.question: What is the core claim made in this passage?
questions.answer: The prescribed prayers are a sacred summary and guide to the many forms of worship found across all creation.

questions.question: How is the human being characterized in relation to the larger creation?
questions.answer: As a smaller model of the whole universe.

questions.question: How is Surah al-Fatihah characterized in relation to the Qur’an?
questions.answer: As a bright summary or sample of the entire Qur’an.

questions.question: Based on those two examples, what role do the prescribed prayers play?
questions.answer: They serve as a complete and illuminating summary of worship.

questions.question: What two images are used to explain the nature of the prescribed prayers?
questions.answer: The images of an index and a map.

questions.question: What is being gathered by the prayers when they are called an index?
questions.answer: The many types of worship.

questions.question: What is being pointed out by the prayers when they are called a map?
questions.answer: The different forms and levels of worship found among created beings.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the connection between the five daily prayers and the rest of creation?
questions.answer: The prayers are tied to a much wider pattern of devotion that extends through all creatures.

questions.question: What three things are compared in this passage?
questions.answer: The human being to the universe, Surah al-Fatihah to the Qur’an, and the prescribed prayers to all forms of worship.

questions.question: Why are these comparisons grouped together?
questions.answer: They all show how a smaller thing can contain and reflect the meaning of a larger whole.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the structure of the prescribed prayers?
questions.answer: Their structure is comprehensive enough to include many dimensions of worship.

questions.question: What does the phrase about all classes of creatures add to the meaning?
questions.answer: It broadens the idea of worship beyond human beings to the whole created world.

questions.question: Why might the passage call the prayers a shining or luminous guide?
questions.answer: Because they help reveal hidden spiritual meanings and direct the worshipper toward them.

questions.question: What is the central message of the passage in one sentence?
questions.answer: The prescribed prayers are a concentrated representation of the worship woven throughout all creation.

questions.question: What is the best summary of the passage for a college student?
questions.answer: Salah is a compact but powerful act that gathers and points to the worship of the whole creation.

questions.question: What is the first analogy given before the prayers are discussed directly?
questions.answer: A person is compared to a miniature version of the universe.

questions.question: What is the second analogy given before the prayers are discussed directly?
questions.answer: Surah al-Fatihah is compared to a concise representation of the whole Qur’an.
